findings.title: immediateDelete path never deletes the DB reminder row
findings.body: When immediateDelete is true, the function cancels the batch at SendGrid and returns without deleting the workflowReminder row. On reschedule, the old reminders therefore stay in the database. Unscheduled reminders (scheduled=false) will later be picked up by the cron and sent for the old booking time. Each cancellation also adds a pending entry to SendGrid's scheduled_sends, which is capped at 100, so this path brings back the limit the PR is meant to avoid.

findings.title: Cron still schedules reminders already marked cancelled
findings.body: The query for unscheduled reminders does not filter out cancelled=true. A reminder for a cancelled booking that has no referenceId yet will be scheduled with SendGrid and sent. The cancel step only handles reminders scheduled within the next hour, and by then the email has already been queued.

findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch
findings.body: The loop over cancelled reminders sits inside a single try/catch. If any SendGrid request throws (for example because referenceId is null or the 100-pending limit is hit), the remaining reminders are skipped. The delete promises collected so far are also never awaited, so those rows stay in the database.

findings.title: Cancelled reminders already past their date are deleted before cancellation runs
findings.body: The deleteMany at the top runs first and removes rows whose scheduledDate is already past. A cancelled reminder whose date fell between cron runs (the cron runs every 15 minutes) is deleted without ever being cancelled at SendGrid. The email is then sent.

findings.title: Workflow delete skips unscheduled reminders and leaves SendGrid cancels pending
findings.body: Reminders are queried with scheduled=true only, and the email path uses immediateDelete, which does not remove the row. The cascade delete of the workflow cleans up the rows, but every scheduled email still triggers an immediate SendGrid cancel. Deleting a large workflow can therefore exhaust the 100 pending-cancellation limit the PR set out to avoid.
